first.rationale: Current competitive pressure on price-sensitive SMB segments directly mirrors the scenario where memory_73 showed promotional pricing drove strong acquisition and revenue lift. Memory_31 and memory_86 both demonstrated activation and onboarding improvements, but those are operational lifts we've already captured. The 6% activation decline and 4% onboarding decline suggest execution or friction issues rather than missing mechanics. The immediate threat is competitive win-loss on price-sensitive accounts. Verifying memory_73 (targeted promotional pricing effectiveness) will confirm whether a precision pricing intervention can recapture market share while protecting margin through targeting. Memory_31 will validate whether the onboarding simplification from day 12 is still holding or if decay explains current drops. A standard experiment with SMB price-sensitive cohorts running a limited-time promotional offer addresses the acute competitive threat while the verification clarifies whether we've regressed on earlier gains. This preserves long-term value by defending qualified SMB revenue rather than chasing low-intent volume, and avoids enterprise sales motion which would consume resources we don't have capacity to scale this week.
